title: Accidental accuracy and vertex corrections in $GW$: Exact benchmarks for the extended Hubbard model
abstract: The $GW$ approximation is the standard tool for quasiparticle predictions in materials, yet its regime of validity in correlated systems remains poorly quantified, because \textit{ab initio} vertex corrections are computationally prohibitive. Using exact diagonalization of the half-filled extended Hubbard model on finite rings as a numerically exact reference, we construct the corresponding model-space $GW$ theory on the identical Hilbert space and quantify its error as a function of local ($U$) and non-local ($V$) interaction strength. We find that the vertex correction changes character across the phase diagram: in the weak-coupling regime the effective vertex $Γ_{\rm eff} < 1$, reflecting the suppression of RPA charge fluctuations by exact short-range correlations, whereas in the Mott regime $Γ_{\rm eff}$ grows monotonically (to $\sim 3$ for $N=6$, reflecting the local vertex required to open the Hubbard gap. Vertex corrections in the electron-hole (polarizability) channel are shown to \emph{worsen} the gap error, indicating that the Mott gap resides in the self-energy channel. For $V=0$, static $COHSEX$ is accidentally exact at a single crossover point $U^* \approx 3.5\,t$; finite $V$, through non-local Fock exchange, splits this point into a double-crossover window that collapses toward weak coupling. These results yield quantitative diagnostics for the reliability of $GW$ in correlated materials.
summary: This work rigorously benchmarks the GW approximation against exact diagonalization for the extended Hubbard model. It finds that the approximation fails to correctly predict the Mott gap, quantifying the necessary vertex correction ($\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$) which varies significantly across the phase diagram. The results establish quantitative criteria for assessing the reliability of GW in strongly correlated electronic systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to quantify the reliability and error of the GW approximation for quasiparticle predictions in correlated materials, specifically addressing the role of vertex corrections.
main_result: The effective vertex correction ($\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$) changes character across the phase diagram: it is $<1$ in the weak-coupling regime but grows large in the Mott regime, indicating that standard GW fails to capture the full gap opening.
method: The authors benchmark GW theory against numerically exact results obtained via exact diagonalization (ED) of the extended Hubbard model on finite rings.
model_or_system: The study uses the half-filled extended Hubbard model, described by a Hamiltonian including on-site ($U$) and nearest-neighbor ($V$) interactions, studied on finite rings.
key_observables: Effective vertex ($\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$), quasiparticle gap ($\Delta$), and the comparison between ED and GW calculated gaps.
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($U, V$), finite size ($N=6, 10$), and the crossover point $U^*$.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the static limit (COHSEX) for the self-energy and focuses on the spin-integrated density-channel functional.
figures_summary: Figures compare the exact ED gap versus the GW gap, show the dependence of $\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$ on $U$, and illustrate how non-local interactions split the accidental crossover point.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the failure of GW in different regimes, first establishing the ED benchmark, then diagnosing the failure via $\Gamma_{	ext{eff}}$, and finally showing how non-local interactions complicate the picture.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of correlation effects, gap opening, and the failure of simple approximations like GW provides crucial theoretical diagnostics for understanding strongly correlated quantum materials.
